correctness.rationale: The Bochner–Schoenberg cosine basis reduces the universal positivity question to each integer input frequency. Integration by parts gives the exact cosine coefficients for degree≤3 Bernstein polynomials. For necessity, cos(t) gives opposite signs in the zeroth coefficient and high even Fourier tail unless the quadratic midpoint or cubic reflected-node condition holds. For sufficiency, every input frequency of each parity has explicit coefficients; the difficult odd cubic bracket is bounded below by 2π²−16 or 8 for all positive odd output frequencies. The constant generator is preserved; uniform absolute convergence handles arbitrary positive-definite inputs. A standalone Python checker ran 35,102 auxiliary coefficient comparisons; the infinite statement does not depend on those finite tests.

value.rationale: The cone of circle-isotropic positive semidefinite kernels is a natural covariance-preservation constraint. The complete two-degree classification settles the first nontrivial flexibility question for endpoint-fixed Bernstein sampling: the degree-two grid is forced to be uniform while degree-three grids contain a full continuum of nonuniform admissible choices. This is structurally informative for selecting interpolation nodes, beyond the already-known single uniform sample grid.
